title: Clara Blanche Telfer/Lane (1883–1974)

# Clara Blanche Telfer (1883–1974)

**Born:** 18 November 1883 — Tantanoola, South Australia
**Died:** 5 June 1974 — South Australia
**Father:** [[John Telfer (1840–1913)]]
**Mother:** [[Martha Clara Henstridge (1856–1921)]]
**Spouse:** Francis Edward Lane (m. 6 April 1903, d. 1940)

## Life Summary

Clara Blanche Telfer was born on 18 November 1883, the tenth child of John Telfer (1840–1913) and his second wife Martha Clara Henstridge. She married Francis Edward Lane on 6 April 1903 at the Tantanoola Presbyterian Church. The marriage certificate listed Francis's occupation as "Hotel Keeper" — he was the Licensee of the Tantanoola Tiger Hotel from 1902 to 1905, together with his brother William Lane.

Clara and Francis had ten children, though three died in infancy: Edna Elizabeth Lane (lived nine months), Brenda Olive Lane (lived three months), and Francis Lane (lived two days). The seven who survived were Nina Amy, Ethel Jean, Derrice Elma, Edna Mary, Doris Elizabeth, Albin Edward John and June.

Clara had a very close relationship with her brothers and sisters and often visited Tantanoola. In her 90th year she made a special request to be driven to the Presbyterian Church where she had been married, and to other places which held very special memories. She died five months after this visit, on 5 June 1974.

Francis Edward Lane died in 1940 at the age of 74.

## Family Stories

Clara Blanche was the tenth child of John Telfer — the last of his daughters — born in 1883 at Tantanoola. At nineteen she married Francis Edward Lane, a hotel keeper who ran the Tantanoola Tiger Hotel with his brother. The wedding took place at the Tantanoola Presbyterian Church on 6 April 1903.

She raised seven surviving children through hard times. Her brother Roland never married and was a great friend of Clara and her family, spending every Good Friday and Christmas Day with them for decades.

In her 90th year, Clara returned to Tantanoola for a visit and asked to be driven to the Presbyterian Church where she had been married all those years before, and to other places that held special memories. She died five months later, on 5 June 1974 — ninety years old, and the last surviving child of John and Martha.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp.249–251)*
